title: Zeer Pot Evaporative Cooler
problem_description: Vegetables and dairy spoiling due to no refrigeration in hot dry climate
solution_summary: Two nested unglazed clay pots with wet sand between them. Evaporation of water through the outer pot wall creates a 10-15°C temperature drop inside. Works best in hot arid conditions, ineffective in monsoon humidity.
materials_json: [{"item": "Large clay matka (outer)", "quantity": "1", "cost_inr": 120, "source": "pottery_market"}, {"item": "Smaller clay matka (inner)", "quantity": "1", "cost_inr": 80, "source": "pottery_market"}, {"item": "Clean sand", "quantity": "2 kg", "cost_inr": 0, "source": "free"}, {"item": "Wet jute cloth (lid)", "quantity": "1", "cost_inr": 30, "source": "agriculture_shop"}]
build_steps_json: ["Place larger matka in a shaded, ventilated spot", "Fill bottom with 5cm of sand, add water until damp", "Place smaller matka inside", "Pack wet sand in the gap between the two pots", "Cover inner pot opening with wet jute cloth", "Re-water the sand twice daily", "Store vegetables in inner pot"]
failure_modes: If humidity > 60%, cooling effect drops to near zero — switch to underground pit storage instead. If sand dries out completely, effectiveness drops immediately — water twice daily.

title: Motorcycle Engine Water Pump
problem_description: Irrigation pump motor failed, need to water 2-acre field, no budget for new pump
solution_summary: Attach a centrifugal pump head to a motorcycle's rear wheel drive using a shaft coupler. The motorcycle engine provides 8-12 HP, enough to pump 20,000 litres/hour from a well or canal up to 10 meters head.
materials_json: [{"item": "Centrifugal pump head (1.5 inch)", "quantity": "1", "cost_inr": 800, "source": "agriculture_shop"}, {"item": "Shaft coupler (motorcycle axle to pump)", "quantity": "1", "cost_inr": 300, "source": "local_welder"}, {"item": "PVC pipe 1.5 inch", "quantity": "5 metres", "cost_inr": 200, "source": "hardware_store"}, {"item": "Pipe fittings and connectors", "quantity": "4 pieces", "cost_inr": 100, "source": "hardware_store"}]
build_steps_json: ["Remove motorcycle rear wheel, keep engine running on centre stand", "Weld or clamp shaft coupler onto rear axle stub", "Mount pump head aligned with axle — village welder can do this in 1 hour", "Connect inlet pipe from water source with foot valve at bottom", "Connect outlet pipe to field distribution channel", "Start motorcycle at low RPM, gradually increase to operating speed", "Pump delivers ~20,000 L/hour at 1500 RPM"]
failure_modes: If pump doesn't prime: ensure foot valve is submerged and inlet pipe has no air leaks. If vibration is excessive: check shaft alignment with a straight edge. If motorcycle overheats: run at lower RPM, allow cooling breaks every 30 minutes.

title: Neem Oil + Sticky Trap Integrated Pest System
problem_description: Aphid and whitefly infestation on vegetable crop, no chemical pesticides available or affordable
solution_summary: Two-part system: neem oil spray disrupts pest reproduction cycle (works on larvae and eggs), yellow sticky traps catch adult flying insects. Together effective against 80% of common crop pests at <₹200 for a 0.5-acre plot.
materials_json: [{"item": "Neem cake or neem leaves", "quantity": "500g", "cost_inr": 0, "source": "free_local_tree"}, {"item": "Mild soap (any brand)", "quantity": "50ml", "cost_inr": 10, "source": "local_shop"}, {"item": "Yellow plastic sheets or yellow paint", "quantity": "4 pieces", "cost_inr": 40, "source": "hardware_store"}, {"item": "Mustard oil or motor grease (sticky coating)", "quantity": "100ml", "cost_inr": 20, "source": "local_shop"}, {"item": "Bamboo sticks for trap posts", "quantity": "4", "cost_inr": 0, "source": "free"}]
build_steps_json: ["Boil 500g neem leaves in 5L water for 20 minutes, cool and strain", "Add 5ml soap to strained neem water — soap helps oil stick to leaves", "Spray on all crop surfaces at sunset (UV destroys neem oil in sunlight)", "Cut yellow plastic sheets 30x30cm, coat with old motor grease or mustard oil", "Mount on bamboo sticks at crop canopy height", "Replace sticky traps when covered with insects (typically 1-2 weeks)", "Repeat neem spray every 7-10 days"]
failure_modes: Neem spray ineffective if applied in sunlight — always spray at dusk. If infestation persists after 3 applications, increase concentration. Yellow traps don't catch crawling pests — combine with neem drench at soil level for root aphids.

title: Brick and Sand Solar Fruit/Vegetable Dryer
problem_description: Excess produce going to waste, no electricity for mechanical drying, need to extend shelf life
solution_summary: A low-cost indirect solar dryer made from bricks, a black-painted sheet, and a mosquito net drying rack. Raises internal temperature to 50-60°C, drying most produce in 2-3 days. Indirect design prevents UV damage to nutrients.
materials_json: [{"item": "Old bricks", "quantity": "20", "cost_inr": 0, "source": "free_scrap"}, {"item": "Black plastic sheet or black painted metal sheet", "quantity": "1 sqm", "cost_inr": 50, "source": "hardware_store"}, {"item": "Mosquito net or jali", "quantity": "1 sqm", "cost_inr": 80, "source": "local_shop"}, {"item": "Bamboo or wooden frame", "quantity": "4 rods", "cost_inr": 0, "source": "free"}, {"item": "Clear plastic sheet (roof)", "quantity": "1.5 sqm", "cost_inr": 60, "source": "hardware_store"}]
build_steps_json: ["Build a 60x40cm brick enclosure, two bricks high, south-facing", "Place black sheet on the floor of enclosure (solar collector)", "Build a wooden/bamboo frame over the enclosure", "Stretch mosquito net across the frame as drying rack", "Cover with clear plastic sheet angled to face sun", "Leave 5cm gaps at sides for airflow", "Place sliced produce on net rack", "Cover with another net layer to keep insects out"]
failure_modes: Ineffective during monsoon — humidity prevents evaporation. If drying is uneven: turn produce halfway through. If mould appears: increase airflow gaps, reduce layer thickness.

title: Biogas Digester from Plastic Drum
problem_description: No cooking gas connection, LPG too expensive, have cattle dung available daily
solution_summary: A simple fixed-dome biogas digester using two 200L plastic drums. Produces 1-2 hours of cooking gas daily from 5kg cattle dung. Digested slurry is high-quality organic fertiliser. Payback in 3-4 months vs LPG cost.
materials_json: [{"item": "200L plastic drum (inlet)", "quantity": "1", "cost_inr": 400, "source": "kabadiwala"}, {"item": "200L plastic drum (gas holder)", "quantity": "1", "cost_inr": 400, "source": "kabadiwala"}, {"item": "PVC pipe half-inch", "quantity": "3 metres", "cost_inr": 90, "source": "hardware_store"}, {"item": "PVC fittings, valves", "quantity": "1 set", "cost_inr": 150, "source": "hardware_store"}, {"item": "Rubber tube for gas line", "quantity": "2 metres", "cost_inr": 60, "source": "hardware_store"}]
build_steps_json: ["Bury inlet drum 80% underground, leaving top 40cm above soil", "Connect inlet pipe at bottom — this is where you add dung+water slurry", "Invert gas holder drum over inlet drum — it floats up as gas fills it", "Connect gas outlet pipe from top of gas holder to kitchen", "Add valve on gas line to control flow", "Initial charge: mix 5kg dung with 10L water, pour in daily for 15 days", "Gas production starts in 10-15 days", "Daily operation: add 5kg dung + 10L water each morning"]
failure_modes: Low gas pressure: check for leaks with soapy water on all joints. No gas after 20 days: increase dung ratio, check temperature (needs >15°C). Slurry overflowing: reduce daily input volume.
